description: I'm Daniel, a civil engineering graduate interested in terrain mapping, photogrammetry, and web development. Our team,ENDURANCE ATLAS , is building an interactive map of Mount Sharp for Interplanetary Survival Guide: Martian Map. We want users to explore the terrain, compare routes, and spot hazards along the way. Join us if you enjoy working with GIS, 3D visualization, web development, planetary science, or UX design.
summary:
Marswalk Gale is a 3D web app for planning and rehearsing an astronaut walk across the boxwork ridges of Mount Sharp in Gale Crater, using real NASA data.

What we built: We built an interactive planner on top of real Mars terrain from the MRO HiRISE elevation model and orthoimage. The planner lets the crew overlay these data layers:

slope
THEMIS thermal inertia from Mars Odyssey
Curiosity’s REMS weather, RAD radiation readings, Navcam views and traverse
NASA DONKI space-weather alerts
details:
Marswalk Gale is a 3D web app for planning and rehearsing an astronaut walk across the boxwork ridges of Mount Sharp, Gale Crater. It has two modes.

  1. Planner. It loads the real Martian terrain from the MRO HiRISE elevation model and orthoimage. The crew can overlay these data layers:
    A route algorithm (Dijkstra on the terrain grid) finds the safest path between science stops. It checks every walk against an oxygen, time and energy budget. Each stop gets a proposed science task, based on whether it sits on a ridge or a hollow.
    • slope
    • Mars Odyssey THEMIS thermal inertia
    • Curiosity’s REMS weather, RAD radiation, Navcam images and traverse
    • NASA DONKI space-weather events
  2. Helmet view. It replays the walk in first person, with a HUD and a minimap. TARS, a simulated AI agent on the suit, talks with the astronaut, watches modeled vital signs and oxygen, and gives directions. When a solar alert arrives, TARS shows how many minutes the return takes, recommends going back, and lets the astronaut decide.

Benefits

  • One tool for many data sources: orbital, rover and space-weather data together, so the crew doesn’t have to check them separately.
  • Honest data: every value is labeled Observation, Derived or Model.
  • Easy to use: runs in any browser with no installation, in English and Spanish.

Intended impact

Future Mars crews will have little margin for error. Marswalk Gale shows how open NASA data and an onboard assistant can help crews plan safer, more productive walks, and train for decisions before they go outside. It also helps students and the public explore real Mars data.

Tools and technologies

  • Languages: JavaScript, HTML, CSS, Python.
  • 3D and web: Three.js and Vite.
  • Data pipeline: Python scripts that download and process the NASA datasets (about 22 MB in total).
  • Testing and the demo video: Playwright and FFmpeg.
  • Hosting: GitHub and GitHub Pages, deployed automatically.
  • Hardware: a standard personal computer; no special hardware needed.

Creativity

  • It combines a mission-planning tool with a first-person helmet simulation, so the crew both plans a walk and rehearses it.
  • TARS turns raw data into a conversation and a clear decision (“return now or continue?”) instead of a list of numbers.
  • An animated intro tells the mission’s story.

Factors we considered

  • Safety first: slope, thermal, radiation and space-weather risk, with a safety margin for the return.
  • Life-support limits: oxygen, time and energy.
  • Science value: each stop has a purpose.
  • Data honesty: estimates are never shown as measurements.
  • Accessibility and performance: works in the browser, in two languages, and on ordinary computers.
  • Security: the public version has no API keys, so TARS runs as a local simulation.
